title: King Oliver recommends Lester to Red Allen; Prez named by Billie Holiday
summary: Phillips tells how Oliver told Red Allen in Nashville about Lester, Allen's doubts versus Hawkins, and how Billie Holiday later named him Prez.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Let me ask you this. So you're talking about Lester Young's development and as he went on through different stages of his career. When he was playing with King Oliver, you said King Oliver gave him a lot of space on a lot of tunes, like "Tiger Rag." Did King Oliver ever have any statements about Lester Young's style?
Yeah.
Tell me about that. And anything he would have told Lester as a leader to his sidemen.
Yeah, he told Red Allen, in Nashville, Tennessee.
Trumpeter Red Allen.
Yeah. Red was with Fletcher Henderson. Lester wasn't with us then. We'd just left him in Kansas City.
He'd quit?
Yeah, he was gone. See, he promised...
This was in 1933?
He promised King anyway that he'd play with him that season, but he couldn't go down to Nashville on this regular job we went on every year.
He promised he'd play with them where?
Up until about November.
November 1933?
Phillips - 134
Yeah.
Then what happened?

Then he left... We left him in Kansas City. He went with Andy Kirk, I think it was. It probably was Andy Kirk. I think it was Andy Kirk. Then when we got down in Nashville, we run into Fletcher Henderson.
What month was this in 1933?

November, or something like that. Close to Christmas. We usually went down there every year and stayed three months, down in Ridgeway and Nashville, Tennessee. Red told King, "Man, Hawk is going over in Europe; I see they want him over there." King said, "Man, they got a tenor player in Kansas City, you'all ought to try to get him. He'll fill any place playing." So Red said, "He ain't no Hawk, is he?" King said, "No, he ain't no Hawk, and Hawk ain't he. Ain't no one he either." He said, "You will like him 'cause he sure can play." After that, Red Allen came here with Lucky Millinder. Red Elkins(?) knew him, and said "Red, what did you think of Lester?"
This was after Lester had played briefly with Fletcher Henderson.
Right. He said, "Oh, he was all right, but he wasn't no Hawk." Red said, "I know he's not no Hawk." He said, "Prez will set Hawk down in a jam session and blow him clear out the room!"
Phillips - 135
That's what Red Elkins said.
That's what he told Red Allen.
Then what did Red Allen say to that?

He said, "Maybe so, but I don't believe it. Man, that's the Hawk!" He said, "Yeah, but you'all ain't listenin' to this cat, man. He can play. You just don't change what he's doing. He's doing something that other tenor players ain't never played. You don't hear that kind of sound on tenor, and what he's playing."
So when Les came back out here with Basie, he saw Red Allen again. "What did you think now, Red?"
Who was asking him that?
Red Elkins. Because they used to play together in New York. "Well, he says..."
This was in D.C.?
Yeah.
Because Red, you and Pete Jones were in D.C.
Yeah.
So this was around 1937.
Something like that, yeah.
What did he say this time?

"Well, all right. He's a good man, all right." He still had to come on in, but he didn't want to come in like he's supposed to come in. He was talkin' then... There was cats who'd asked about Les, asking me and Pete about
Phillips - 136

him. "Hey, man, what have you heard from Les? When Basie gonna be comin' back?" You know what I mean? I said, "I don't know, man, when they're coming back. But you'll see placards on the bulletin board when they come in." "Yeah, man, I want to hear that cat, man. That cat is something, the tenor player."

So that's the way it went on, you know. And from then on, it was Prez. Then Billie Holiday named him Prez. Billie Holiday said, "He is the President of the Tenor Saxophone." So there ain't no question about it. And he was. Hawk and them could play, but Hawk and them played that slow tenor. To me... It was all right. Ballads. Hawk on a ballad, he was fine to me. But if you put a tune up in tempo, he was jagged. He wasn't smooth like Prez. You got "Clap Hands, Here Comes Charlie." Smooth. See how smooth he played that? It's way up in tempo.
